title: Cinder & Reed Festival 2027: performer laminate passes — neutralize eight mixed-light headshots to an in-frame grey card, triage-prep the three access-tier marks, then data-merge one press-ready laminate per performer

source.reference: InDesign Data Merge - festival performer credential / laminate passes

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork event-credential brief (an events team wanting personalised backstage/performer passes produced from a lineup list against a designer-built InDesign template) and laundered to a fictional brand, 'Cinder & Reed Festival' — no real festival, venue, artist, sponsor, person, or trademark is named anywhere; performer and stage names are invented. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the killed original merged into a convert_pdf_to_indd output (which will NOT bind merge fields) and relied on a data-merge image field that cannot exist in a converted PDF. The corrected design supplies a genuinely hand-authored InDesign single-record laminate template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> AND TWO @-prefixed image-path columns (one for the performer headshot, one for the access-tier mark). document_merge_data_layout emits exactly ONE FILE PER ROW, so a per-performer single-record laminate is the correct, connector-doable shape (one pass per performer), not a multi-up sheet. The client is modeled as supplying: the authored .indd, the lineup roster CSV, eight raw performer headshots shot by different stage photographers under mismatched light each with a photographic 18% grey card laid in frame, and the three access-tier marks (two flat two-colour crests and one photograph of a printed holographic foil sample). The Adobe chain does the real work the brief rewards: neutralize every headshot to its own in-frame grey card so the whole credential set shares one white point and prints sharp, triage the three tier marks so each is prepped the correct way (the flat crests vectorized for razor edges, the photographed holographic mark knocked to transparency and kept as high-res raster rather than destroyed by a trace), then run the authored template through a one-file-per-row data-merge and export a press-ready laminate per performer.
one_line_ask: Neutralize eight mixed-lighting performer headshots to the 18% grey card each one carries so the credential set reads as one matched, print-sharp series, decide per frame how far to move white balance and exposure to hit the shared target, prep the three access-tier marks each the correct way for print (the flat crests are not the same problem as the photographed holographic mark), then data-merge the client's authored single-record InDesign laminate template against the lineup roster to produce one press-ready pass per performer.
full_brief: Cinder & Reed Festival 2027 is a two-stage boutique showcase, and we need the physical performer laminate passes produced from our confirmed lineup — one personalised pass per performer, worn on a lanyard, that has to look sharp and consistent on stage and on camera. Our brand and the pass layout are already signed off; what we need is the production. We are handing you everything the job needs. First, the headshots: eight performer photos, but here is the problem — they were shot by different stage photographers across load-in and soundcheck under whatever light was around (some under cool LED wash, some under warm tungsten, one under greenish work-lights, a couple over- or under-exposed), so straight out of the folder they look like eight different shoots. A row of passes where every face has a different colour cast looks amateur. To make this checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. Your job on the photos: bring every headshot to one consistent, true-to-skin look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set shares one white point and one exposure feel. Do NOT force one blanket correction across all eight: each was lit differently and needs its own white-balance and exposure decision to land on the shared target — some frames need warming, others need cooling, and pushing the same numbers through all of them will leave the set mismatched. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame, and the final pixel size of each headshot, so we can confirm the set is matched and that every face will still be sharp at print size. That last part matters: each pass drops the headshot into a 60 x 75 mm photo window, and at press resolution that window needs at least ~709 x 886 px of real image — a face cropped down to a small web thumbnail will print soft and blurry, which we will reject. Second, the access-tier marks: three of them sit on the passes depending on the performer's tier — two are flat two-colour crests (ARTIST and SUPPORT), and the third, the AAA all-access mark, is a photograph of our printed holographic foil sample with all its sheen and rainbow gradient. All three need to be prepped so they drop cleanly into the pass's mark window and stay sharp at print size — but they are not the same kind of file and should not be treated the same way; think about which one can become clean line art and which one cannot survive that. Finally, build the passes: we have hand-built the InDesign laminate template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (headshot and tier mark), and we are giving you the lineup roster; merge them so every performer gets their own single pass with their name, stage and access tier bound in, their neutralized headshot dropped into the photo window, and their tier mark in the mark window — then hand back a press-ready ~300 DPI PDF, one pass per performer. Bind the names, stages and tiers verbatim from the roster — do not invent or reassign anyone; some performer names are long and must fit the auto-size name frame without clipping. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point; every headshot at least ~709 x 886 px so it prints >=300 DPI in the 60 x 75 mm window; the three tier marks each prepped the correct way and razor-sharp at print size; and exactly one finished laminate per roster row.

inputs.name: cinder_reed_laminate_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD 100 x 140 mm portrait performer laminate pass with 3 mm bleed — ONE performer per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<FullName>>, <<Stage>>, <<AccessTier>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a 60 x 75 mm portrait photo window bound to @Portrait, and a 20 x 20 mm square mark window bound to @TierBadge. The <<FullName>> text frame has Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so long performer names bind without going overset. The festival crest/masthead and the tier colour band are already drawn into the template artwork (fixed on every pass), so the only per-row imagery is the headshot and the tier mark. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output: a converted-PDF template has no live merge fields and no data-merge image field, so it would not bind — which is exactly the defect this rebuild removes.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record per-performer laminate is the correct, connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. Two image columns (@Portrait, @TierBadge) mean the merge must resolve two prepped assets per row. Column names must exactly match the roster headers.

inputs.name: performer_lineup.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: FullName,Stage,AccessTier,@Portrait,@TierBadge and 8 performer rows (one per confirmed act). FullName is a mix of realistic international stage/performer names including at least two DELIBERATELY LONG names (e.g. 'Anneliese Vandermeulen-Okonkwo', ~28+ chars) alongside short ones so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. Stage is one of exactly two fictional stage names: 'The Foundry' or 'Reed Room'. AccessTier is one of exactly three values: AAA, Artist, Support. @Portrait holds the agreed prepped headshot filename for that performer (portrait_p1_final.jpg ... portrait_p8_final.jpg, in row order) so the data-merge drops the correct neutralized headshot into that pass. @TierBadge holds the prepped tier-mark filename mapped from AccessTier: AAA -> badge_aaa.png, Artist -> badge_artist.svg, Support -> badge_support.svg. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<FullName>>,<<Stage>>,<<AccessTier>> and the two @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight finished laminates (page-count = row-count gate). The @Portrait / @TierBadge columns hold the filenames the agent must produce and upload under those exact names, so naming discipline is a real dependency. The AccessTier->@TierBadge mapping means the AAA rows resolve to the raster holographic mark while Artist/Support rows resolve to the vector crests — proving the two image columns and the triage both land in the deliverable. Long names exercise the auto-fit frame.

inputs.name: raw_performer_headshots_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 photoreal candid performer headshots, upper-body portraits of different fictional musicians backstage / at soundcheck, each with a photographic 18% grey card clipped at one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, all on a similar neutral-grey backstage backdrop. Shot under mismatched light so no single correction fits: (1) cool blue LED stage-wash cast; (2) warm orange tungsten cast; (3) greenish fluorescent work-light cast AND slightly underexposed; (4) overexposed near-daylight, highlights hot on the forehead; (5) near-neutral but flat and low-contrast; (6) strong cool blue window-shade cast AND dark/underexposed; (7) mixed warm-key/cool-fill, mildly off; (8) slightly warm and dull. Each portrait has real skin texture, hair detail and fabric, a candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI; the grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in every frame; rendered large (roughly 2000 x 2500 px) so there is headroom to crop the card out and still clear the print pixel floor.
inputs.realism_notes: Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB and exposure vary, in opposite directions) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own decision measured to its in-frame 18% grey card, the free checkable neutral target (inputs are generated, so it costs nothing). Rendered oversized so the correct crop to the 60 x 75 mm window stays above the ~709 x 886 px print floor; a naive small web crop would fall below 300 DPI. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable JPEGs; the grey card is cropped out for the final pass.

inputs.name: badge_artist_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat two-colour access-tier crest reading 'ARTIST' — solid deep-ink lettering and a simple emblem on a solid single-colour block, high contrast, hard clean edges, no gradients, no sheen, no photographic texture, exported slightly oversized and off-centre with a thin margin. Looks like printable line art / a logo file.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat, high-contrast, solid-fill so image_vectorize yields a clean SVG after prep-before-trace (crop-to-bounds + crisp). One of the two marks that CAN become clean vector line art.

inputs.name: badge_support_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat two-colour access-tier crest reading 'SUPPORT' — solid lettering and a simple emblem on a solid single-colour block, high contrast, hard clean edges, no gradients, no sheen, no photographic texture, exported a different non-square size from the ARTIST mark with a thin margin.
inputs.realism_notes: Second flat vector-ready mark; different export size from the ARTIST mark so the crop-to-bounds prep is genuinely needed to normalise both before tracing.

inputs.name: badge_aaa_holo.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A close-up PHOTOGRAPH of a printed holographic foil access laminate sample reading 'AAA', shot on a dark surface: a shiny metallic rainbow-gradient foil with specular highlights, reflections, subtle surface texture and smooth colour transitions across the letters and background. Clearly a photographed glossy object, not flat line art — full of gradients and sheen.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRIAGE / TRAP asset. It looks like 'just another tier mark', but it is a photographed holographic surface full of gradients and specular sheen: feeding it to image_vectorize returns a flat, muddy silhouette that destroys the foil look. The correct treatment is crop-to-bounds -> image_remove_background to transparency -> keep as a high-resolution raster placed via @TierBadge. Getting it wrong is invisible in a thumbnail and only shows when the AAA passes print flat and dead.

outputs.name: CinderReed_Laminates_perPerformer_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready 100 x 140 mm portrait performer laminate passes — ONE single-record pass per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge with 3 mm bleed and crop marks at ~300 DPI; each pass binds its FullName/Stage/AccessTier verbatim from the roster, drops that performer's grey-card-neutralized headshot into the 60 x 75 mm photo window (>=709 x 886 px so it prints >=300 DPI), and drops the correct prepped tier mark into the 20 x 20 mm mark window (vector crest for Artist/Support rows, transparent-ground holographic raster for AAA rows).

outputs.name: headshots_neutralized_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized, consistently cropped performer headshots, each with its in-frame 18% grey card driven to a clean neutral and the whole set matched to one shared white point and exposure feel while staying true-to-skin (no face pushed off its real colour); each cropped to the 60 x 75 mm photo-window ratio and kept at >=709 x 886 px. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move AND the final pixel dimensions of each frame.

outputs.name: tier_marks_prepped
outputs.spec: The three access-tier marks prepped triage-correct: badge_artist.svg and badge_support.svg as clean vector line art traced only after crop-to-bounds + crisp prep, and badge_aaa.png as the photographed holographic mark cropped and knocked to transparency then kept as a high-resolution raster (>=236 px square) — NOT vectorized, so the foil sheen survives to print.

connector_workflow.note: Cool blue LED cast: WARM it (positive temperature) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey and skin reads true. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card — do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast / _vibrance_and_saturation).

Crop the grey card out and reframe on the subject to the 60 x 75 mm (4:5) photo-window ratio, keeping the result at >=709 x 886 px so it clears the 300 DPI print floor. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand. Report final px.

Warm tungsten cast: this frame must move the OPPOSITE direction from frame 1 — COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and it matches the shared white point. Adaptive: the batch is not uniformly cool, so a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=709 x 886 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Greenish fluorescent cast AND underexposed: the dominant colour move is on TINT (push toward magenta) to kill the green while neutralizing the grey card, plus a real exposure lift — a two-axis problem, not a simple temperature slide. Land the card neutral on the shared white point. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=709 x 886 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Overexposed near-daylight with hot forehead highlights: PULL exposure/highlights/whites down to recover the blown skin first, then a small WB nudge so its grey card lands neutral on the shared white point. Tonal recovery dominates here. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=709 x 886 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Near-neutral light but flat and low-contrast: its grey card is already close to neutral, so only a SMALL WB nudge is needed to sit on the shared white point — over-correcting would push it off the set. The real work is tonal: add contrast/clarity and a touch of vibrance to match the set's feel without clipping. Report the (small WB, tonal) move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=709 x 886 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Strong cool blue window-shade cast AND dark: warm STRONGLY and lift shadows/exposure to bring it up while neutralizing its grey card to the shared white point; protect skin from going muddy. The biggest correction in the set — proof that identical batch numbers cannot serve every frame. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=709 x 886 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.
Mixed warm-key / cool-fill, only mildly off: a modest, careful correction to bring the grey card to neutral on the shared white point without overshooting. Report the move.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=709 x 886 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Slightly warm and dull: cool a touch to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point and add vibrance/clarity to match the set. Report the move. Frames 1-8 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 4:5 photo window at >=709 x 886 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px.

Triage: the ARTIST mark is flat two-colour line art, so it CAN become clean vector. Prep-before-trace step 1: crop the oversized/off-centre export to the tight bounds of the mark so the trace sees only the crest, not the margin.
Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast and set the black/white points so the two solid colours separate hard-edged — a soft or low-contrast raster traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Trace the prepared flat mark into a clean SVG so the ARTIST crest stays razor-sharp at the 20 mm mark window across every Artist-tier pass.
The SUPPORT mark is also flat line art (different export size). Prep-before-trace step 1: crop to the tight bounds of the mark.
Prep-before-trace step 2: crisp the contrast/black point so the trace is clean-edged, matching the ARTIST mark's treatment.
Trace the prepared SUPPORT mark into a clean SVG for the Support-tier passes.

Triage DIVERGES here: the AAA mark is a PHOTOGRAPH of a holographic foil sample — full of gradients and specular sheen — so it CANNOT become clean line art (vectorizing it would return a flat muddy silhouette and kill the foil). Crop only to the tight bounds of the mark; do NOT send it to image_vectorize.

Knock the dark surround to transparency so only the holographic AAA mark remains, keeping every gradient and highlight intact. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill, NOT a solid fill). This preserves the foil the vector path would have destroyed.

Square-crop/resize the transparent holographic mark to the 20 x 20 mm (1:1) mark-window ratio at >=236 px square so it prints >=300 DPI. Kept as a high-resolution raster placed via @TierBadge for the AAA rows. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: portrait_p1_final, portrait_p2_final, portrait_p3_final, portrait_p4_final, portrait_p5_final, portrait_p6_final, portrait_p7_final, portrait_p8_final, badge_artist.svg, badge_support.svg, badge_aaa.png
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the eight grey-card-neutralized headshots plus the three prepped tier marks so the merge can resolve them by the @Portrait and @TierBadge columns. Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @Portrait / @TierBadge columns resolve to for each performer's single-record pass.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (FullName/Stage/AccessTier) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and drop that row's neutralized headshot into the @Portrait frame AND its mapped tier mark into the @TierBadge frame — producing EXACTLY ONE merged pass per row (eight passes); the auto-fit name frame shrinks long names. [T] requires the hand-authored template. A convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-up sheet would not bind / cannot be produced — this is the corrected merge path.

Export the merged single-record passes to a press-ready ~300 DPI 100 x 140 mm + 3 mm bleed PDF with crop marks, one pass per performer. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. Eight per-headshot grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization (adaptive per frame: warm the cool LED frame 1, cool the tungsten frame 2, magenta-tint+lift the green/dark frame 3, recover the overexposed frame 4, hold WB but add tone on the flat frame 5, strongly warm+lift the blue/dark frame 6, modestly correct the mixed frame 7, cool+vibrance the warm/dull frame 8) followed by an image_crop_and_resize that crops the grey card out, reframes to the 4:5 photo window and holds >=709 x 886 px — every neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame 18% grey card so all eight converge on one shared white point. The three access-tier marks TRIAGE into two paths: the flat ARTIST and SUPPORT crests each run crop_to_bounds -> crisp adjustments -> image_vectorize into clean SVGs (17->18->19, 20->21->22), while the photographed holographic AAA mark diverges to crop_to_bounds -> image_remove_background (transparency) -> crop_and_resize into a high-res transparent raster (23->24->25), deliberately never touching image_vectorize. The eight final headshots and the three prepped marks converge into the upload session(26) -> finalize(27) -> document_merge_data_layout(28), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and emits one merged pass per row, resolving BOTH @Portrait and @TierBadge per row. The merged set is exported to the per-performer press PDF(29). Nothing after the raw loads originates outside the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 29 connector calls, 9 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/prep/vectorize/knockout, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 upload steps. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision in a different direction (cool frames warmed, warm frames cooled, one green/dark frame fixed on a second axis, one overexposed frame tonally recovered, one already-neutral frame held on WB but lifted tonally) all forced to converge on a single measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass, and every crop must additionally clear a numeric print-DPI floor (>=709 x 886 px in the 60 x 75 mm window). Layered on top is a genuine two-way triage of three superficially-similar tier marks (flat crests vectorized after prep-before-trace; a photographed holographic mark knocked to transparency and kept as raster, NOT traced) whose wrong treatment is invisible until print, and a two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (the template is a supplied authored .indd); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; image_fill_area and image_apply_color_overlay are unused; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _vibrance_and_saturation / _brightness_and_contrast are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE: every headshot carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance criterion is that each finished card reads a clean neutral with the whole set matched to one white point — a target the agent can miss — and the agent must REPORT the final white-balance/exposure move AND final pixel size per frame so 'matched' and 'sharp' are verifiable rather than asserted; two further checkable gates back this: each headshot crop must clear >=709 x 886 px (so it prints >=300 DPI in the 60 x 75 mm window), and the merged PDF page-count must equal the roster row-count (8), since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit headshots to a common measurable white point, each needing its own opposite-direction correction, plus the numeric DPI floor on every crop; (2) a two-way triage of three superficially-identical access-tier marks that require DIFFERENT correct treatments — the flat ARTIST/SUPPORT crests prepped-and-vectorized to clean line art, the photographed holographic AAA mark knocked to transparency and kept as high-res raster because a trace would flatten its foil — a mistake invisible until the AAA passes print dead. TRAP: the AAA holographic mark looks like 'just another tier crest', so the naive path sends all three marks through the same crop->vectorize pipeline; vectorizing the holographic photo returns a flat muddy silhouette that passes as a thumbnail but destroys the foil at print, while the correct path routes only the two flat marks to image_vectorize and takes the holographic one through remove_background-to-transparency. A second pitfall sits in the grade (pushing identical batch numbers through all eight differently-lit frames leaves the set mismatched) and in the merge (a convert_pdf_to_indd or multi-up template will not bind — only the supplied single-record authored .indd merges). MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE: every grey card neutral and the set on one white point with per-frame WB/exposure reported; every headshot >=709 x 886 px with final px reported; the three tier marks prepped triage-correct (two clean vectors, one transparent-ground raster >=236 px); and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI 100 x 140 mm pass per roster row.
